content.intro: M5: Energy Governance for a Just Energy Transition

content.text: Inclusive and effective institutions are the cornerstone of robust governance systems, ensuring coordinated efforts for a just energy transition. This section explores the roles of key actors, multi-level governance, and the importance of transparency, trust, and anti-corruption measures in energy governance.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Integrated Governance for a Just Energy Transition
lessons.description: This lesson explores the transition from centralized, state-led energy management to decentralized, multi-stakeholder governance, emphasizing collaboration across governments, regulatory bodies, private sector actors, and civil society to ensure transparent, inclusive, and adaptive energy transitions.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Civic Engagements And Its Role in Energy Governance
lessons.description: This lesson explores the role of civic engagement in energy governance, highlighting how participatory decision-making, energy democracy, and community-driven initiatives enhance transparency, accountability, and public trust while fostering localized solutions and equitable energy transitions.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Facilitating Cooperation with a Heterogeneous Civil Society
lessons.description: This lesson explores the mechanisms for effective civic engagement in energy governance to empower diverse civil society actors—local communities, women, youth, and indigenous peoples—in driving a just and sustainable energy transition.
